Chapter 6 of Applied Statistical Modelling for Ecologists, by Marc Kéry and Kenneth Kellner, considers the case of two predictors in a linear regression model. Traditionally this would be a t-test, comparing two means across groups defined by one categorical predictor, but here we extend it to include an additional continuous predictor.

```{julia}
using RCall, DataFrames, StatsPlots

R"""
set.seed(61)
n1 <- 60
n2 <- 40
μ1 <- 105.0
μ2 <- 77.5
σ <- 2.75

n <- n1 + n2
y1 <- rnorm(n1, μ1, σ)
y2 <- rnorm(n2, μ2, σ)
y <- c(y1, y2)

x<- rep(c(0, 1), c(n1, n2))
"""
x = @rget x
y = @rget y
```

```{julia}
using GLM

y_obs = DataFrame(y = y, x = x)
model = lm(@formula(y ~ x), y_obs)
model
```

```{julia}
using HypothesisTests

t_test_result = EqualVarianceTTest(y_obs.y[x .== 0], y_obs.y[x .== 1])
t_test_result
```

```{julia}
using Turing, FlexiChains, MCMCDiagnosticTools

@model function linear_model(y, x)
    α ~ Normal(0, 100)
    β ~ Normal(0, 100)
    σ ~ truncated(Cauchy(0, 10); lower=0)

    μ = @. α + β * x
    y ~ product_distribution(Normal.(μ, σ))
end

model_turing = linear_model(y_obs.y, y_obs.x)
chains = sample(model_turing, NUTS(), MCMCThreads(), 1000, 4; progress=false)
summarystats(chains)
```

### Trace plots
```{julia}
plot(chains; size = (800, 600))
```

```{julia}
α_post = vec(Array(chains[:α]))
β_post  = vec(Array(chains[:β]))
σ_post = vec(Array(chains[:σ]))

mu2 = mean(α_post .+ β_post )
```
